source.title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on the simplex S^{m-1}, given by x'k = x_k (1 + sum_i a_{ki} x_i) where A = (a_{ij}) is skew-symmetric and |a_{ij}| <= 1, determine whether there exist Lyapunov functions beyond the three families already known in the paper: multiplicative monomials of the form x_1^{p_1} ... x_m^{p_m} with p_i >= 0 and sum_i p_i = 1, coordinate sums sum_{i=r+1}^m x_i under the stated sign condition on the coefficients, and coordinate ratios x_i / x_j.
accepted.context_brief: New Lyapunov functions for Volterra QSOs

evidence.quote: Theorem 1. [10],[14] For the Volterra QSO (7) the following assertions hold 1) For the dynamical system (7) there exists a Lyapunov function of the form ϕp (x) = x1p1 ...xpmm , where pi ≥ 0, m i=1 pi = 1 and x = (x1 , ..., xm ) ∈ intS m−1 . 2) If there is r ∈ {1, ..., m} such that aij < 0 ... then ϕ(x) = m i=r+1 xi ... is a Lyapunov function for QSO (7). 3) There are Lyapunov functions of the form ϕ(x) = xi/xj , i 6= j, x ∈ intS m−1 .
Problem 1. Does there exist another kind of Lyapunov function for QSO (7)?

accepted.question_text: Generalize the notion of transversality from Volterra quadratic stochastic operators to arbitrary quadratic stochastic operators V(x) with heredity coefficients P_{ij,k}. In particular, define what it should mean for a non-Volterra or arbitrary QSO to be transversal, and then find necessary and sufficient conditions on the cubic heredity matrix P = (P_{ij,k}) that exactly characterize when the operator is transversal.

evidence.quote: A skew-symmetric matrix A is called transversal if all even order leading (principal) minors are nonzero. A Volterra QSO V is called transversal if the corresponding skew-symmetric matrix A is transversal [14],[18],[36].
Problem 2. Define concept of transversality for arbitrary QSO and find necessary and sufficient condition on matrix P = (Pij,k ) of a QSO under which the QSO is a transversal.

accepted.question_text: For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator whose set X of fixed points is finite, let U = U_1 ∪ ... ∪ U_t be a neighborhood decomposition around the fixed points x_1, ..., x_t, and for a trajectory x^(0), x^(1), ... define its itinerary as the sequence n_1, n_2, ... recording which neighborhood U_{n_s} is visited successively. Determine whether there exists a trajectory whose itinerary is periodic.

evidence.quote: Thus the trajectory firstly visits the neighborhood of a fixed point xn1 then it visits the neighborhood of a fixed point xn2 and so on. The sequence n1 , n2 , ... is called the itinerary (route-march) of the trajectory x(0) , x(1) , ...
Problem 3. Is there a trajectory with periodic itinerary?

accepted.question_text: Consider the three-dimensional Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^2 defined by x' = x (1 + a y - b z), y' = y (1 - a x + c z), z' = z (1 + b x - c y), where a, b, c are in [-1,1]. The paper proves that if a, b, and c are all nonzero and have the same sign, then the ergodic theorem fails for this operator. Determine whether one can formulate a sufficient condition for the ergodic theorem to hold for this family, and in particular whether the parameter-sign condition appearing in Theorem 3 is sharp for separating ergodic and non-ergodic behavior.
accepted.context_brief: Ergodicity for the three-parameter Volterra family

evidence.quote: V : S2 → S2  x′ = x (1 + ay − bz) , y ′ = y (1 − ax + cz) , z ′ = z (1 + bx − cy) , where a, b, c ∈ [−1, 1].
Theorem 3. [3] If the parameters a, b, c for the Volterra QSO (9) have the same sign and each is non-zero, then the ergodic theorem will fail for this operator.
Problem 4. Is the condition of Theorem 3 sufficient for the ergodic theorem to hold?

accepted.question_text: For a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^{m-1} written in the form x'k = x_k (1 + sum_i a_{ki} x_i) with skew-symmetric coefficient matrix A = (a_{ij}), find necessary and sufficient conditions on A under which the ergodic theorem holds, meaning that the Cesàro averages (1/n) sum_{k=0}^{n-1} V^k(x) exist for every initial state x in the simplex.
accepted.context_brief: Matrix criterion for ergodicity of Volterra QSOs

evidence.quote: On the basis of numerical calculations Ulam [44] conjectured that ergodic theorem holds for any QSO V , that is, the limit limn→∞ 1/n ∑_{k=0}^{n-1} V k (x) exists for any x ∈ S m−1 .
Problem 5. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on matrix A of Volterra QSO under which the ergodic theorem is true for the Volterra QSO on S m−1 , m ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: Let τ be a permutation of the species indices and let V_τ be the permuted Volterra quadratic stochastic operator obtained from a Volterra QSO by permuting coordinates according to τ, so that for τ not equal to the identity the operator is non-Volterra. Determine the asymptotic behavior of trajectories of V_τ for arbitrary permutations τ, including the structure of omega-limit sets, convergence, periodic behavior, or other long-term dynamics.

evidence.quote: Let τ be a cyclic permutation on the set of indices 1, 2, ..., m and let V be a Volterra QSO. Define QSO Vτ by ... Note that QSO Vτ is a non-Volterra QSO iff τ ≠ id.
Problem 6. Investigate the asymptotic behavior of the trajectories of the operators Vτ (automorphisms) for an arbitrary permutation τ .

accepted.question_text: For a fixed ℓ, an ℓ-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator is a QSO in which offspring type restrictions are Volterra-like for species 1 through ℓ but allow genuinely non-Volterra behavior for species ℓ+1 through m. Classify all periodic trajectories of a given ℓ-Volterra QSO, not just the vertex cycles whose existence is guaranteed by Proposition 1.

evidence.quote: Definition 2. For any fixed ℓ ∈ E, the QSO defined by (4), (5), (11) and (11a) is called ℓ-Volterra QSO.
Proposition 1.[41] 1) For any set Is = {ei1 , ..., eis } ⊂ {eℓ+1 , ..., em }, s ≤ m, there exists a family Vℓ (Is ) ⊂ Vℓ such that Is is an s-cycle for every V ∈ Vℓ (Is ).
Problem 7. Find the set of all periodic trajectories of a given ℓ−Volterra QSO.

accepted.question_text: Develop a general dynamical-systems theory for ℓ-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators. This should include, at minimum, the construction of Lyapunov functions for ℓ-Volterra QSOs, a description of the limit sets of their trajectories, and other core structural results about their asymptotic dynamics.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Develop theory of dynamical systems generated by a ℓ-Volterra QSO. Find its Lyapunov functions, the set of limit points of its trajectories etc.

accepted.question_text: Given two quadratic stochastic operators V_1 and V_2 on the same simplex, study how the dynamical properties of the convex combination V_λ = λ V_1 + (1 - λ) V_2 for λ in [0,1] depend on and relate to the properties of V_1 and V_2. In particular, determine which features of trajectories, invariant sets, fixed points, attractors, or irregular behavior persist, disappear, or emerge under this interpolation.
accepted.context_brief: Dynamics under convex combinations of QSOs

evidence.quote: In [15] it was considered the following family of QSOs Vλ : S 2 → S 2 : Vλ = λV0 + (1 − λ)V1 , 0 ≤ λ ≤ 1 ... Thus properties of Vλ change depending on the parameter λ.
Problem 9. For arbitrary two QSOs V1 and V2 connect the properties of Vλ = λV1 + (1 − λ)V2 , λ ∈ [0, 1] with properties of V1 and V2 .

accepted.question_text: Let ξ = {E_1, ..., E_q} be a partition of the species set E, and define a ξ-QSO by requiring P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever both parent indices i and j lie in the same block E_p. Determine whether an analogue of Theorem 5 holds for every ξ-QSO; that is, whether such operators always have a unique fixed point and whether every trajectory converges to it, as happens for F-QSOs.
accepted.context_brief: Analogue of F-QSO theorem for ξ-QSOs

evidence.quote: Theorem 5. [39] Any F -QSO has a unique fixed point (1, 0, ..., 0) (with m zeros). Besides, for any x0 ∈ S m , the trajectory {x(n) } tends to this fixed point exponentially rapidly.

Problem 10. Consider a partition ξ = {E1 , ..., Eq } of E i.e., E = E1 ∪...∪Eq , Ei ∩Ej = ∅, i 6= j. Assume Pij,k = 0 if i, j ∈ Ep , for p = 1, ..., q. Call the corresponding operator a ξ−QSO. Is an analogue of Theorem 5 true for any ξ−QSO?

accepted.question_text: For strictly non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators, the paper proves in dimension m = 3 that every operator of the form (14) has a unique fixed point, that this fixed point is not attractive, and that the operator can exhibit 2-cycles and 3-cycles depending on parameters. Determine whether the same conclusions remain true for strictly non-Volterra QSOs in dimensions m >= 4.

evidence.quote: Theorem 6. [40] 1) For any values of parameters a, b, c, d, α, β with (15) the operator (14) has a unique fixed point. Moreover the fixed point is not attractive. 2) The QSO (14) has 2-cycles and 3-cycles depending on the parameters (15).
Problem 11. Is Theorem 6 true for m ≥ 4?

accepted.question_text: For each dimension m, let α_m be the smallest constant such that every quadratic stochastic operator V on S^{m-1} satisfying P_{ij,k} > α_m for all heredity coefficients is regular. The paper states that if P_{ij,k} > 1/(2m), then V is regular, and it gives the exact value of α_2. Determine the exact value of α_m for every m >= 3.

evidence.quote: In [17] the authors consider an arbitrary QSO V : S m−1 → S m−1 with matrix P = (Pij,k ) and studied the problem of finding the smallest αm such that the condition Pij,k > αm implies the regularity of V . Theorem 7. [17] 1) If Pij,k > 1/2m then V is regular. 2) α2 = 1/2 (3 − √7).
Problem 12. Find exact values of αm for any m ≥ 3.

accepted.question_text: A continuous operator V on the simplex S^{m-1} is called bistochastic when V(x) is majorized by x for every x. Investigate the trajectory behavior of bistochastic quadratic stochastic operators: describe their long-term dynamics, possible limit sets, convergence or non-convergence patterns, and how the majorization constraint shapes the orbit structure.

evidence.quote: Definition 4. An arbitrary continuous operator V : S m−1 → S m−1 satisfying the condition V (x) ≺ x, x ∈ S m−1 is called a bistochastic operator.
Problem 13. Investigate the behavior of trajectories of the bistochastic quadratic operators.

accepted.question_text: Describe and classify all surjective quadratic stochastic operators on the simplex S^{m-1} in every dimension m >= 5.

evidence.quote: In [5] and [28] a description of surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for m = 2, 3, 4 and classification of extreme points of the set of such operators are given.
Problem 14. Describe the set of all surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for any m ≥ 5.

accepted.question_text: Consider the graph-and-measure construction of a quadratic stochastic operator V_μ in which a finite graph G, an allele set Φ, a positive probability measure μ on the configuration space Ω, and heredity coefficients P_{σ_1 σ_2,σ} defined by formula (17) produce a QSO by formula (18). Determine exactly which quadratic stochastic operators arise from this construction, and characterize the class of all QSOs obtainable in this way.
accepted.context_brief: Characterize QSOs arising from the graph construction

evidence.quote: The QSO V ≡ Vµ acting on the simplex S(L, Φ) and determined by coefficients (17) is defined as follows ... for any cell σ ∈ Ω.
Note that the construction above does not give all possible QSOs. So the following problem is interesting. Problem 15. Describe the class of QSOs which can be obtained by the construction.

accepted.question_text: When a quadratic stochastic operator is generated by a Gibbs measure associated with a Hamiltonian H on a continuous state space, and when the underlying statistical-mechanical system may undergo a phase transition because the Gibbs measure is non-unique, determine how the thermodynamic behavior, especially phase transitions, affects the trajectories and asymptotic dynamics of the corresponding QSO.
accepted.context_brief: Effect of phase transitions on QSO dynamics

evidence.quote: More precisely, if E is continual set then one can associate the Gibbs measure µ by a Hamiltonian H (defined on E) and temperature T > 0 [37]. It is known that depending on the Hamiltonian and the values of the temperature the measure µ can be non unique. In this case there is a phase transition of the physical system with the Hamiltonian H.
Problem 16. (by N.N.Ganikhodjaev) How the thermodynamics (the phase transition) will effect to behavior of the trajectories of a QSO corresponding to a Gibbs measure of the Hamiltonian H?

accepted.question_text: Describe the class of non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operators that can be decomposed or reduced to several separate Volterra quadratic stochastic operators, in the sense illustrated by Theorem 11 for operators generated from product measures on disconnected graphs.

evidence.quote: Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 17. Describe the set of all non-Volterra QSOs which are reducible to several Volterra QSOs.

accepted.question_text: Find a probability measure μ on the configuration space that is different from the product measure μ(σ) = product_i μ_i(σ_i) in formula (19), but for which the associated non-Volterra quadratic stochastic operator can still be analyzed within the framework of the existing theory of quadratic stochastic operators, analogous to how Theorem 11 reduces the product-measure case to separate Volterra QSOs.
accepted.context_brief: Non-product measures still tractable by QSO theory

evidence.quote: Consider probability measure µ on Ω = Ω1 × . . . × Ωq defined by µ(σ) = ∏_{i=1}^q µi (σi ) ... Theorem 11. [38] The QSO constructed by the construction (18) with respect to measure (19) is reducible to q separate Volterra QSOs.
Problem 18. Find a measure µ different from (19) such that the non-Volterra QSO corresponding to µ can be investigated in the framework of a well known theory of QSOs.

accepted.question_text: Find a class of quadratic stochastic operators for which the set of initial states whose trajectories have historic behavior has positive Lebesgue measure, where historic behavior means that for some continuous function f on the simplex the time averages (1/(n+1)) sum_{i=0}^n f(V^i(x)) fail to converge.

evidence.quote: We say that a trajectory {x, V (x), V 2 (x), ...} has historic behavior if for some continuous function f : S m−1 → R the average 1/(n+1) ∑_{i=0}^n f (V i (x)) does not exist.
Problem 19. Find a class of QSOs such that the set of initial states which give rise to trajectories with historic behavior has positive Lebesque measure.

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory for quadratic stochastic operators whose heredity coefficients factor as P_{ij,k} = a_{ik} b_{jk}, equivalently operators of the form (V(x))_k = (A(x))_k · (B(x))_k where A(x) and B(x) are linear maps determined by the matrices A = (a_{ik}) and B = (b_{jk}) subject to the stochasticity constraints. Study their structural and dynamical properties as a generalization of Volterra QSOs.
accepted.context_brief: QSOs defined by factorized heredity coefficients

evidence.quote: Consider QSO (4), (5) with additional condition Pij,k = aik bjk , ∀i, j, k ∈ E ... Then the QSO V corresponding to the coefficients (20) has the form x′k = (V (x))k = (A(x))k · (B(x))k .
Problem 20. Develop theory of QSOs defined by (21).

accepted.question_text: Classify all quadratic stochastic operators V on S^{m-1} for which there exists an integer r >= 2 such that V^r(x) = V(x) for every x in the simplex.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Describe all QSOs which satisfy V r (x) = V (x) for any x ∈ S m−1 and some r ≥ 2.

accepted.question_text: For the topological conjugacy classification of quadratic stochastic operators, determine whether there exists a finite complete system of indicator polynomials in the heredity coefficients P_{ij,k}. If such a system exists, find a basis, where an indicator is a polynomial constrained by topological conjugacy and a complete system is one whose bounds imply that two QSOs are topologically conjugate.
accepted.context_brief: Finite complete indicator systems for conjugacy

evidence.quote: Definition 6. A polynomial f (Pij,k ) is called an indicator if from the topologically conjugateness of V1 and V2 it follows that ... Definition 7. A system f1 , ..., ft of indicators is called complete if ... A minimal complete system of indicators is called a basis.
Problem 22. Does there exist a finite complete system of indicators? Find the basis of the system of indicators.
